reason: Read with the c. 1481 breviary at hand, worn words that the image-only reading left unresolved ('Felix sabbatum?', 'assp[.]iebat', 'ce?ehmie') were read as 'Felix salutacio', 'aspernebat' and 'celerrime cupiebat', and the faded lesson on slip 1r could be followed.

text:
F-wbkk (Stams, Stiftsarchiv, Frg. 260). Source-assisted reading, 31 October 2026, made with the Breviarium Romanum, about 1481 (BSB Ink B-835, scan 114) and the Cantus Database inventory of Utrecht 406 at hand. A research reader reread every inked line of slips 1, 2 and 3 on the native images, slip 1r on a blue-channel equalised crop. An independent checker reread slips 1r and 2v on the image. Slip 4 is blank on both faces. Not a verified transcription.
Conventions: expansions in ( ), lost or supplied text in [ ], ? doubtful, / line break, [red] rubric. Boxes are left,top,right,bottom in native pixels (7360 x 4912). Canvas 0 (Stams_STA_Frg_260_01r04r) shows the faces pencilled r, canvas 1 (Stams_STA_Frg_260_01v04v) the faces pencilled v. The readings "p(ro)spere" and "temp(t)auit" on 1v agree with the catalogue note and are not independent of it.
